title: Detail room: $0 storage plan and barcode lookup prototype
tagline: Room layout in SketchUp and a working inventory mockup (React, SQLite, Code 128 labels)
summary: I planned a small detail room for dense bin storage using only equipment the shop already owned, and designed a barcode workflow so any employee could find a part. Management approved the layout and agreed with the barcode approach; room construction kept it from being installed before I left.
role: I was responsible for the room plan, the workflow design and refining the mockup; the code was written with an AI assistant.
goal_constraints:
- Fit dense storage into a small room, with every part findable by anyone.
- High-variety, low-quantity parts: depleted items often aren't restocked, so bins get reused.
- Use equipment the shop already owned.
process_md:
- Planned the room in SketchUp: two rolling Uline bin racks that wheel out for full access, three LISTA cabinets, a computer table, and space for a cart or filing cabinet. Base layout $0; a third rack would add $760, or $900–1,090 with bins.
- Designed the workflow: every bin gets a permanent location label and every part type a code; scanning a part and then a bin label links them. The system doesn't detect where parts are, so a part found in the wrong bin gets relinked.
- Refined a working mockup built with AI coding help: search a part to see its total and bins, link by scanning, a front view of each rack, Code 128 label printing, and a history log. Scanner and printer are simulated on screen.
- Researched budget hardware: USB scanners, Raspberry Pi, old Android devices, and a DIY handheld (Wio Terminal + Zebra LS1203).
- Showed it to the lead engineer's assistant (positive feedback).

media.caption: Searching "6203 bearing" finds the part, its total stock and both bins it's linked to (sample data).

The small computer room planned as a detail room, using only equipment the shop already owned: two rolling bin racks that wheel out for full access, three LISTA cabinets, a computer table, and a spot for a cart or filing cabinet.
Scan and place: scan the part, then the bin's location label, then confirm. The scans are simulated on screen but go through the same lookup a real scanner would use.
Storage map: a front view of each rack; click a bin to see which parts are linked to it.
